arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Rowe argued the water flow through the dams is a discharge.
Mr. Kayatta argued the river is a single body of water.
Mr. Minear argued the term discharge means flowing out.
Justice Scalia asked if the water is unchanged below the dam.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The case tests whether water flowing through a dam is a discharge. This status triggers state water-quality certification requirements.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: S. D. Warren wants the Court to rule that water passing through its dams is not a discharge.
Maine and the United States want the Court to rule that water passing through the dams is a discharge.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: S. D. Warren argues the river is a single body of water. It claims moving water through a dam is not a discharge into that same body.
Maine and the United States argue the term discharge means flowing out. They claim operating the dams results in a discharge into navigable waters.

sections.heading: What the justices asked
paragraphs: Justice Stevens asked if the water has a slightly different chemical composition.
Chief Justice Roberts asked if the water is a discharge even if it is the same water.
